title: Destiny2FootageSegment
description: Segment-level record: one shot/beat range of a Bungie official Destiny video, tagged along every retrieval axis for natural-language search. PROVENANCE PATTERN: flat fields + parallel provenance map. All tagged fields are plain typed values at the top level of the record; every tagged field SHOULD have a matching entry in `provenance` keyed by the exact field name, with {source, label_source, confidence}. `source`: 'observed' = tagged from the segment's own frames/audio; 'inherited' = copied from the parent video record's video-scoped defaults (era, activity, content_type, destination, subclass_version). `label_source`: manual | heuristic | model. `confidence`: 0..1. Convention for multi-value fields (faction, composition, camera_movement, mood, action): use an empty array when the axis is genuinely not present in the shot; use ['unknown'] only when tagging was attempted but could not be determined; do not mix 'unknown' with other values. DERIVED FIELDS (all label_source 'heuristic', all pure functions of tagged fields, none requiring a model call): `clean` = overlays contains none of {hud, nameplates, burned_text, talking_head} and is the PRIMARY gate — only clean shots get cut into the story; `footage_tier` = cinematic | gameplay | mixed, from content_type, keeping gameplay in the index but beneath cinematics; `traversal_hero` = action includes 'traversal' AND shot_scale in {ELS,LS,MLS,MS} AND camera_movement excludes 'handheld_shaky'; `casting` = the lead/ensemble decision (see $defs/casting).

segment_id.description: Stable unique identifier for this segment within the index.

video_id.description: Identifier of the parent video record (see video.schema.json).

start_tc.description: Start of the shot/beat range as a timecode string, mm:ss or HH:MM:SS.

end_tc.description: End of the shot/beat range as a timecode string, mm:ss or HH:MM:SS.

start_sec.description: Start of the range in seconds (numeric, for indexing).

end_sec.description: End of the range in seconds (numeric, for indexing). Must be greater than start_sec (cross-field constraint enforced by the indexer, not by this schema).

overlays.description: OBSERVED. Overlays burned into the frame, which no edit can remove. Tag ['none'] (or []) for a frame with nothing burned in. 'hud', 'nameplates', 'burned_text' and 'talking_head' are DISQUALIFYING: they make `clean` false. 'letterbox' is a warning only — bars can be cropped. See vocab/cleanliness.yaml.

clean.description: DERIVED gate, and the project's primary filter: true iff `overlays` contains none of {hud, nameplates, burned_text, talking_head}, i.e. the shot can be cut into the story as-is. An ABSENT or untagged `overlays` derives clean=false — cleanliness must be positively established, because a false positive puts a HUD in the finished cut. label_source should be 'heuristic'.

footage_tier.description: DERIVED cutting tier from content_type: {cinematic,cutscene}->'cinematic', gameplay->'gameplay', otherwise 'mixed'. Gameplay is kept in the index but ranked beneath cinematics, so a story defaults to the cinematic look and falls back to gameplay for coverage. label_source should be 'heuristic'.

class.description: Guardian class of the subject. 'unknown' when no class can be told (e.g. back-only wide shots of a fireteam).

element.description: Light/Darkness element visibly expressed (ability FX, weapon FX, subclass color language).

faction.description: Enemy faction(s) visible in the shot (multi). Empty array when no enemy faction appears; ['unknown'] only when indeterminate.

shot_scale.description: Shot scale: ELS/LS/MLS/MS/MCU/CU/ECU, INSERT for object insert shots, UNKNOWN when indeterminate.

camera_movement.description: Camera movement(s) present (multi). 'handheld_shaky' matters because it excludes traversal_hero.

substitutability.description: How comfortably this shot's subject reads as 'could be anyone'. 0 = a specific named character, unmistakable; 5 = fully anonymous/interchangeable. INDEPENDENT of shot_scale: a CU on a featureless helmet can still score 4-5. DEMOTED to a tie-breaker between otherwise-equal clean ensemble shots — it is NOT a usability gate, since a face-clear lead is fully usable at 0.

identity_visibility.description: How much of the subject's identity-revealing surface is visible. 'face_obscured' includes full helmets; 'none' = no person in frame.

character_identifiability.description: Whether the specific character can be named: explicit = unmistakably a named character; inferred = deducible from context; implied_by_costume = class/armor readable but person unknown; unidentifiable = anonymous.

face_count.description: Number of visible (uncovered) faces in frame.

subject_facing_camera.description: Whether the primary subject faces the camera. null when not applicable (e.g. no person in frame).

register.description: Mythic register: -2 grounded/gritty ... 0 neutral ... +2 fully mythic/legendary.

subject_salience.description: What the shot is ABOUT (single, REQUIRED): the Guardian as hero figure; the environment/destination; an enemy threat; an object or artifact; a crowd/group; or ambient texture.

action.description: Action(s) taking place (multi). 'traversal' = running/jumping/parkour/sparrow-free movement through space.

traversal_hero.description: DERIVED boolean: true iff action includes 'traversal' AND shot_scale in {ELS,LS,MLS,MS} AND camera_movement does not include 'handheld_shaky'. Marks the wide, mythic 'Guardian in motion' beats that carry a sequence. label_source should be 'heuristic'.

name.description: Free-text entity name, e.g. 'Zavala', 'The Traveler', 'Eris Morn'.

kind.description: Entity category. Free-text names mean the vocabulary is open-ended; kind only buckets the entity.

character.description: Named entities appearing in the segment. Empty array when no specific named entity is present (anonymous Guardians are NOT characters; they are the substitutable subject).

caption.description: Free-text natural-language description of the segment. This is the embedding-indexed field that carries the long tail beyond the controlled axes.

provenance.description: Parallel provenance map keyed by tagged field name. Convention: every tagged field present on this record SHOULD have a matching entry; keys must be one of the taggable field names below.

role.description: Which casting tier this shot belongs to. 'lead' = a named Destiny character from vocab/casting.yaml `leads` is on screen and is played by a fixed person. 'ensemble' = anonymous Guardian slot(s) fillable from the month's Project Bluefin contributor pool. 'none' = nobody to cast (environment, enemy, artifact).

character.description: Canonical `leads` key matched, e.g. 'elsie_bray' (aka spellings such as 'exo_stranger' normalize to it). null unless role is 'lead'.

person.description: Id of the real person cast. Set for role 'lead' when that character has been cast (null for a lead that is written but not yet cast). ALWAYS null for 'ensemble' at index time: ensemble people are assigned per calendar month by tools/ensemble.py so the pool can rotate without retagging segments.

usable.description: DERIVED. Whether the shot can actually be used for `person`. True for unconstrained leads and for ensemble. For a CONSTRAINED binding (jeefy -> Saladin, which requires far + helmeted framing because the person does not resemble the character) it is false when the shot violates the constraints, and the unmet keys are listed in `constraints_failed`. An unusable shot gets no lead boost and is excluded from that character's retrieval.

constraints_failed.description: DERIVED. Constraint keys the shot fails for a constrained lead binding, e.g. ['require_far','require_helmet'] for a tight, face-clear Saladin. Empty when usable, or when the binding has no constraints.

slots.description: How many contributor credit tiles this shot can carry. 0 for 'lead' and 'none'. For 'ensemble': 6 for a crowd composition, 3 for a group/crowd_group, else 1.

casting.description: DERIVED casting decision. Rule, applied in order: (1) if any name in `character` matches a `leads` key or its aka list -> role='lead', character=that canonical key, person=the binding's person (may be null if uncast), slots=0. Most lead bindings carry no resemblance constraints and are usable at any shot scale, because the project names roles rather than compositing faces; a CONSTRAINED binding (jeefy -> Saladin: far + helmeted only) is evaluated here, setting usable=false and listing the unmet keys in constraints_failed. (2) elif subject_salience in {guardian_hero, crowd_group} -> role='ensemble', character=null, person=null, usable=true, slots per the crowd/group/solo rule. (3) else -> role='none', character=null, person=null, usable=false, slots=0. SHOULD carry a provenance entry with label_source 'heuristic'.

source.description: inherited = copied from the parent video record's video-scoped defaults; observed = tagged from this segment's own frames/audio.

label_source.description: Who/what produced the label: a human (manual), a deterministic rule (heuristic), or an ML model (model).

era.description: Destiny release era. Usually inherited from the video record.

activity.description: Activity type depicted. Usually inherited from the video record; may be observed per-segment when a video mixes activities.

content_type.description: Nature of the footage in THIS segment. Often inherited from the video; override when a trailer video contains gameplay or cinematic shots.

destination.description: Controlled vocabulary of in-fiction Destiny locations. Use 'unknown' when unclear or not in the controlled list.

subclass_version.description: Subclass generation (e.g. arc_3 = Arc 3.0 rework). INHERITED from era via heuristic, NEVER observed from frames: a shot cannot tell a 3.0 subclass from an earlier one.
